implemented: Private live-scope capture and target engine construction preserve app/workspace intent and original readonly history. SDK clients, contexts, agent sessions and handoffs are not transferred.

Actual SDK/Guard reviewed notes enter fresh producer-keyed brokers after fresh policy and file-content checks. A reviewed edit invalidates an earlier capture; explicit pre-import cancellation removes its staged copy.
Semantic stamps exclude capture/manifest bookkeeping but bind all scope, producer, review, original retention and content dependencies. Shared cache clones retain the same root/slot ownership.
Zero-scope metadata generations preserve unmapped source keys and provide no note-read authority. Existing size/retention/three-generation bounds remain.
Historical producer metadata is attached without relabeling prior observations or resetting their timestamps; metadata counts toward existing entry/total bounds.

Bounded actor quiescence closes admission before a barrier and rechecks it at dispatch, blocks maintenance, resumes only a still-live source before stop, and never resumes after shutdown. Atomic queue/pause metadata requires no SDK call.

development_corrections.reason: The fixture incorrectly expected ordinary reads to rewrite the saved manifest. EvidenceSlot.revalidate updates the in-memory observation only. The corrected test requires the source manifest stay byte-identical and semantic data stay unchanged, retaining real review/source-change assertions and all original deadlines.
The first type-check called a backend-private has_cache helper from the builder. Use the already validated scope storage policy instead; no visibility or data boundary was relaxed.

limitations: The P6 central service/profile transaction owner, bounded switch jobs and durable SDK/data selection pointers are not implemented. New engine preparation entry points are not yet wired to Versions controls; production builds explicitly report unused entry-point warnings.

The actual engine test uses a fixture-only settings transition after bounded old-actor shutdown to exercise rebuilt scopes. It does not prove an atomic switch, rollback, process-crash recovery or last-good commit.

Memory-only reviewed notes currently refuse with context_upgrade_data_unsupported. Their ephemeral transfer path, accepted feature/data differences and inactive/unmapped scope migration still need completion.

Per-scope deletion across retained/prepared generations, ready-generation pruning, final source/settings/policy coordination, cancellation/Stop races and disk capacity remain native-owner work before exposing the workflow.

Capture currently performs existing policy/source checks on the old actor. Broader source/workload latency and bounded final-boundary I/O need P9/P10 qualification; the local four-call sample is diagnostic only.
Full native Clippy still fails36 verified unchanged-source diagnostics and reports the unwired entry-point warnings. No lint suppression or unrelated fix was introduced.

Original b47380 and genuine newer approved SDK bytes remain unavailable. Production catalog trust/hosting, installed/frozen/other-platform qualification and complete CLI/HTTP/UI/update-policy controls remain required.
The earlier broker-open transport failure retained in the previous milestone is not resolved by this run; dedicated stress/transport qualification remains required.
Live hooks/profile, running preview, system Python, upstream SDK source, execution approvals, Git staging/history and production catalog qualification were not changed.
